title: Randomized Methods for Kernelized DMD
summary: Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) is a data-driven method related to Koopman operator theory that extracts information about dominant dynamics from data snapshots. In this paper we examine techniques to accelerate the application of DMD to large-scale data sets with an eye on randomized techniques. Randomized techniques exploit low-rank matrix approximations at a much smaller computational cost, therefore permitting the use of increased data set sizes.
